beats.narration_slice: A Black Swan is an event outside normal expectations.
beats.visual: Inside the vertical screen-printed atlas card, a neat field of small white swan silhouettes follows a calm diagonal path while one oversized soot-black swan abruptly enters from the opposite corner, breaking the expected pattern; bone-white ground, storm-blue accents, coarse matte ink grain.
beats.purpose: show an unexpected event appearing outside the established pattern
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide symbolic composition of orderly white swans crossed diagonally by one large black swan entering from upper right, minimal bone-white field
beats.continuity: Begins the subject world directly with the core Black Swan contrast, independent of the opener setting.

beats.visual: A single black swan lands at the center of a compact screen-printed landscape, its impact sending a vermilion fracture ring through bridges, towers, and geometric structures arranged around it; low-angle composition emphasizes scale and disruption.
beats.purpose: show that a Black Swan can have outsized consequences
beats.visual_fingerprint: low-angle impact scene with black swan centered over a vermilion shock fracture spreading through miniature infrastructure
beats.continuity: Transforms the anomalous swan from the prior beat into a force whose consequences radiate outward.

beats.narration_slice: Afterward, people build explanations that make it look predictable.
beats.visual: A tabletop-like pale stone field shows a completed jagged path ending at a black swan; behind the event, precise soot-black arrows and technical construction lines are being retroactively drawn backward to form an apparently tidy route, with one restrained vermilion endpoint.
beats.purpose: show people constructing a neat explanation after the event has already happened
beats.visual_fingerprint: top-down diagrammatic scene of a finished irregular path with backward-added arrows converging neatly on a black swan endpoint
beats.continuity: Moves from the event's impact to the retrospective story people construct around it.

beats.narration_slice: Hindsight hides how surprising it really was.
beats.visual: A torn screen-print veil of orderly forecast lines slides over a chaotic burst beneath it, concealing most of the original vermilion rupture while leaving only one jagged edge visible; close cropped composition with broad matte shadows.
beats.purpose: show hindsight covering up the original surprise
beats.visual_fingerprint: close-up layered composition where a smooth sheet of orderly lines masks a chaotic vermilion burst underneath
beats.continuity: Takes the retrospective explanation from the previous beat and shows it visually obscuring the earlier uncertainty.

beats.narration_slice: The name comes from Europe's old belief that all swans were white.
beats.visual: A simplified old European lakeshore rendered as a flat natural-history scene: several white swans float beneath dark cypress-like silhouettes and pale classical shoreline shapes, arranged symmetrically as if the observed world contains only one kind of swan.
beats.purpose: show the historical assumption that all known swans were white
beats.visual_fingerprint: symmetrical European lakeshore scene with only white swans, distant classical silhouettes, calm frontal viewpoint
beats.continuity: Shifts from abstract hindsight into the historical origin of the Black Swan name.

beats.narration_slice: Then Europeans encountered black swans in Australia.
beats.visual: An Australian shoreline cue with flat eucalyptus silhouettes and a broad water inlet; a black swan stands prominently in shallow water while two tiny soot-black observer silhouettes on the far bank face it in surprise, viewed from a wide side angle.
beats.purpose: show the discovery of black swans in Australia
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide Australian wetland with one black swan foreground right, eucalyptus forms, two distant human observers on opposite bank
beats.continuity: Travels from the European white-swan assumption to the contrasting Australian observation.

beats.narration_slice: One observation shattered a rule that had seemed certain.
beats.visual: A large white circular rule-symbol made from repeated white swan silhouettes occupies the center; one black swan punches through its edge, splitting the circle into angular fragments with a sparse vermilion crack.
beats.purpose: show a single contrary observation destroying a supposedly universal rule
beats.visual_fingerprint: centered circular ring built from white swan silhouettes shattered open by one black swan breaking through the lower-left edge
beats.continuity: Abstracts the Australian discovery into the logical consequence of one counterexample.

beats.narration_slice: Taleb says forecasts can fail the same way.
beats.visual: A thin storm-blue forecast curve advances cleanly across a pale field toward a narrow expected corridor, then a black anomaly shape appears far outside it and the projected line fractures sharply before reaching the edge.
beats.purpose: show a forecast failing when reality falls outside its expected range
beats.visual_fingerprint: minimal horizontal forecast corridor with one smooth line abruptly snapping toward an isolated black anomaly above it
beats.continuity: Carries the shattered-rule idea into the modern domain of prediction and forecasting.

beats.narration_slice: Models usually depend on what has already been observed.
beats.visual: A stack of observed pebble-like data marks sits along the bottom of a technical drawing; precise geometric arcs rise only from those existing marks, forming a model whose entire structure is visibly anchored to the recorded past.
beats.purpose: show models being built from previously observed data
beats.visual_fingerprint: bottom-weighted technical composition with clustered observation marks supporting a fan of precise arcs and geometric projections above
beats.continuity: Explains why the forecast in the previous beat was limited: its structure came from prior observations.

beats.narration_slice: Markets can change through events those models barely considered.
beats.visual: A symbolic market skyline of stacked blocks and bridge-like price structures fills the lower half; an unforeseen soot-black wedge enters from the side and causes several structures to tilt and cascade, while faint model curves remain intact in a distant corner.
beats.purpose: show markets being disrupted by events outside the assumptions of a model
beats.visual_fingerprint: oblique city-market structure collapsing from a black lateral wedge, with faint untouched model curves receding in upper background
beats.continuity: Applies the model limitation from the prior beat to a concrete market system.

beats.narration_slice: Technologies can overturn assumptions just as suddenly.
beats.visual: A row of sturdy mechanical gears and familiar industrial tools occupies one side of the frame while a compact abstract teal device-form drops in from above, abruptly redirecting the entire mechanism so the old gear train breaks apart along a vermilion fault.
beats.purpose: show a new technology suddenly overturning established assumptions
beats.visual_fingerprint: vertical industrial mechanism with old gears on lower left disrupted by a compact teal technological form descending from upper right
beats.continuity: Moves from market disruption to a different domain where unexpected change can overturn established systems.

beats.narration_slice: You cannot reliably predict every Black Swan.
beats.visual: A sparse field of thin probability paths spreads upward like branching tracks, but several terminate at blank edges while a lone black swan silhouette appears in an untouched region beyond all drawn paths; high overhead composition with ample pale stone space.
beats.purpose: show that some consequential possibilities remain outside reliable prediction
beats.visual_fingerprint: high-overhead branching probability paths confined to left side while an isolated black swan sits in uncharted empty space on the far right
beats.continuity: Generalizes the market and technology examples into the limit of prediction itself.

beats.narration_slice: So reduce dependence on fragile forecasts.
beats.visual: A delicate tower balanced on one thin forecast line leans precariously on the left, while on the right a lower, wider structure rests on several independent supports with no single line carrying the whole load; flat architectural screen-print metaphor.
beats.purpose: show the value of not relying on one fragile prediction
beats.visual_fingerprint: split-weight composition contrasting a tall narrow structure balanced on one line with a squat multi-supported structure opposite it
beats.continuity: Turns the limit of prediction into a practical design principle: reduce reliance on any single forecast.

beats.narration_slice: Leave room for error before surprise arrives.
beats.visual: A sturdy bridge-like system spans the frame with visibly unused gaps, spare supports, and open buffer space between structural blocks; in the distance a small black swan approaches, but the system has room to flex without breaking.
beats.purpose: show building buffers and spare capacity before an unexpected shock occurs
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide frontal resilient structure with deliberate empty buffer gaps and redundant supports, tiny approaching black swan in distant upper background
beats.continuity: Completes the practical response by replacing fragile dependence with visible slack and resilience before the next surprise.
